lessons.title: Split observations before learning from them
lessons.motivation: Evaluation must respect the future-use question and unit of independence.
lessons.progression: Compare fixed row split with group/time overlap and final-test-guided selection.
lessons.terms: feature, target, train, validation, test, group, time, random_state.
lessons.worked: A fixed housing split uses 12 training IDs and 4 final-test IDs. Repeated observations from one customer must not be scattered across both sides of a customer-level generalization test.
lessons.misconception: A random seed does not prevent leakage or make every random split appropriate.

objectives.outcome: Choose a split unit consistent with the intended generalization question.
objectives.assessment: Reject an entity/time overlap and explain the unit of independence.
objectives.remediation: Group row IDs by entity/time before splitting.

objectives.outcome: Keep the final test set untouched during preprocessing/model choice.

objectives.remediation: Draw train/validation/test information permissions.

objectives.outcome: Predict a deterministic fixed-ID or seeded split and its limitations.
objectives.assessment: Choose reproducible memberships without claiming representativeness.
objectives.remediation: Compare seed, ordering and split configuration together.

objectives.outcome: Identify feature availability and target timing before modeling.

lessons.title: Fit missing-data rules on training data
lessons.motivation: An imputer learns a rule from training data, then applies that unchanged rule elsewhere.
lessons.progression: Change only test values and verify the training median is unchanged.
lessons.terms: imputer, fit, transform, training statistic, missing indicator.
lessons.math: Training-only medians and conditional missingness assumptions.
lessons.worked: Train ages [10,missing,30] fit median 20. Test ages [1000,missing] transform to [1000,20], not [1000,1000].
lessons.misconception: Imputing before splitting leaks information; a fill value is not an observed fact.

objectives.outcome: Fit imputation statistics using training observations only.
objectives.assessment: Repair a whole-dataset median fit and explain its leakage.
objectives.remediation: Separate fit rows from transform-only rows.

objectives.outcome: Transform new/missing records with the saved training rule.
objectives.assessment: Predict values under a changed test batch.
objectives.remediation: Apply the unchanged fitted statistic explicitly.

objectives.outcome: Choose and justify a missingness policy/indicator for the stated data.
objectives.assessment: Select an appropriate bounded policy and acknowledge its assumption.
objectives.remediation: Compare missing-pattern evidence and possible reasons.

objectives.outcome: Handle all-missing or unexpected columns explicitly.
objectives.assessment: Choose a schema/error policy instead of silently deleting changing columns.
objectives.remediation: Inspect feature names and fitted output schema.

lessons.title: Categorical encoding preserves a feature contract
lessons.motivation: Encoding creates a fitted coordinate vocabulary with an explicit unknown policy.
lessons.progression: Compare a known category with an unseen category and arbitrary integer coding.
lessons.terms: category, ordinal, one-hot encoding, unknown category, fitted vocabulary.
lessons.math: Coordinate representation; arbitrary category codes need not express distance.
lessons.worked: Train plans [basic,pro] with fixed category order [basic,pro] encode basic=[1,0]. With handle_unknown='ignore', unseen team encodes [0,0], an explicit ambiguity rather than a new learned category.
lessons.misconception: Integer category codes do not automatically imply meaningful order; an unknown category must not refit the encoder on test data.

objectives.outcome: Fit vocabulary on training data and apply an explicit unknown-category policy.
objectives.assessment: Repair test refitting and explain the chosen unknown output.
objectives.remediation: Inspect the saved category list and output column names.

objectives.outcome: Predict one-hot output dimensions and column order.
objectives.assessment: Choose the encoding matrix for changed records.
objectives.remediation: Map each category to a named coordinate.

objectives.outcome: Distinguish justified ordinal encoding from arbitrary numbering.
objectives.assessment: Reject a false distance/order claim.
objectives.remediation: Compare category semantics rather than numeric codes.

objectives.outcome: Recognize unknown/drop-reference ambiguity without asserting identical meaning.
objectives.assessment: Choose a cautious interpretation of an all-zero row.
objectives.remediation: Review the encoder's fixed configuration and provenance.

lessons.title: Scaling is a fitted coordinate transformation
lessons.motivation: Scaling learns a coordinate system, not a batch-specific cosmetic adjustment.
lessons.progression: Freeze train mean/scale, then change test values and a constant-feature case.
lessons.terms: mean, standard deviation, StandardScaler, fit/transform, zero variance.
lessons.math: z=(x−μ_train)/σ_train; StandardScaler population variance versus sample variance.
lessons.worked: Train [1,3] has mean 2 and population scale 1, giving [-1,1]. Test value 5 transforms to 3. Its presence must not change the training mean/scale.
lessons.misconception: Scaling is not fitted separately on each test batch; not every mathematical/runtime zero-variance policy is identical.

objectives.outcome: Use training-only scaling statistics and correct denominator.
objectives.assessment: Repair a leaked or sample-denominator scaler and explain its coordinates.
objectives.remediation: Revisit population/sample variance and saved training parameters.

objectives.outcome: Predict transformed values and inverse units.
objectives.assessment: Choose a changed test coordinate under frozen μ/σ.
objectives.remediation: Substitute into the stated transformation.

objectives.outcome: Handle a constant feature according to pinned StandardScaler semantics.
objectives.assessment: Choose its documented scale/output instead of importing old runtime behavior.
objectives.remediation: Compare the library fixture with the separately preserved math-runtime guard.

objectives.outcome: Explain that scaling does not itself prove better generalization.
objectives.assessment: Reject a performance claim based on nicer-looking feature ranges.
objectives.remediation: Separate numerical conditioning from held-out evaluation.

lessons.title: Compose preprocessing without leaking across folds
lessons.motivation: A pipeline controls which data each learned transformation may inspect.
lessons.progression: Start with a two-partition fold primer, then compose typed branches and repeat fitting per fold.
lessons.terms: ColumnTransformer, Pipeline, fitted state, numeric/categorical branch, fold.
lessons.worked: First define a fold as one temporary train/validation partition using two small row-ID lists; no sklearn CV API is assumed. Numeric columns then go through SimpleImputer and StandardScaler; categorical columns through an explicit category imputer and OneHotEncoder. Every learned step sees only that fold's training IDs before transforming validation IDs. S03 later expands this model into repeated folds and API syntax.
lessons.misconception: A Pipeline name alone does not prevent leakage if it receives already-leaked features or was fitted before cross-validation.

objectives.outcome: Choose a correct branch/order and preserve the final feature schema.
objectives.assessment: Repair a swapped encoder/scaler or externally fitted step and justify the order.
objectives.remediation: Trace raw types into each named branch.

objectives.outcome: Fit preprocessing inside each training fold, never on its validation rows.
objectives.assessment: Reject prefit whole-data preprocessing in a fold diagram.
objectives.remediation: Redraw fit/transform arrows per fold.

objectives.outcome: Predict transformed column names/order and output shape.
objectives.assessment: Select the exact joined numeric/categorical feature table.
objectives.remediation: Read branch order and the encoder's fitted vocabulary.

objectives.outcome: Distinguish fit_transform on training data from transform on new data.
objectives.assessment: Repair a second fit on evaluation rows.
objectives.remediation: Track learned attributes before/after each call.

lessons.title: Outlier policies and reproducible preparation reports
lessons.motivation: Outlier handling and reproducibility are recorded policies, not automatic cleanup.
lessons.progression: Compare preserve/investigate/cap plans, then remove a seed-only reproducibility claim.
lessons.terms: outlier, clipping, fitted artifact, seed, provenance, policy, reproducibility.
lessons.math: Robustness, sampling bias and explicit transformation parameters.
lessons.worked: A supplied training-only cap is 50 years; a test age of 80 maps to 50 only under that recorded policy. Choosing a cap after checking which value improves final-test performance is leakage.
lessons.misconception: Outlier removal is not automatic cleaning; a seed alone cannot reproduce missing data/schema/library versions.

objectives.outcome: Choose an outlier policy without test-guided deletion or tuning.
objectives.assessment: Reject a favorable-test-score clipping policy and justify investigation/train-only choice.
objectives.remediation: Trace policy selection data and consequences for population coverage.

objectives.outcome: Record fitted parameters, column order and dataset/version identities.
objectives.assessment: Choose a complete preprocessing report.
objectives.remediation: Compare a new transform with the saved artifact.

objectives.outcome: Separate deterministic seeds from complete reproducibility guarantees.
objectives.assessment: Identify an unpinned ordering/library/data change.
objectives.remediation: Use the environment/data/seed checklist.

objectives.outcome: Explain limitations and abstain on unsupported schema changes.
objectives.assessment: Choose an explicit incompatibility error rather than silently reordering features.
